answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making identity expensive to grow, not just to create. A newcomer may wander into the orchard of tasks, but it earns trust only by finishing small, verified jobs: each success adds a little reputation, while one fraud finding wipes it out. Growing a fake army therefore costs work per identity, like forging ferrous tools one by one, whereas honest agents spread that cost over a long useful life. Copying an identity gains nothing, because reputation sticks to a key's verified history, not to a name that can be duplicated.
